deep.reconstruction:
Setting (my reading of the notation, checked against every step): there are four points P0, P1, P2, P3 in a plane. Gauss uses the symbol (ij) in two ways:
- as a factor, (ij) = r_ij, the length of the segment P_iP_j;
- inside sin and cos, (ij) = φ_ij, the direction angle (azimuth) of the vector P_i→P_j.
So φ_ji = φ_ij + π, and P_j − P_i = r_ij·e^{iφ_ij}. The page carries out the 'development mentioned on p. 150'. That page is not available here, so I do not know which problem it served.

Step 0 (the 'first expression').
Ω = 1/(r01 r23) · {sin(φ02−φ12)cos(φ31−φ03) + sin(φ31−φ03)cos(φ02−φ12)}.
By the addition theorem (my remark) this equals sin(φ02−φ12+φ31−φ03)/(r01 r23).
- φ02−φ12 is the angle at P2 subtending the chord P0P1.
- φ31−φ03 is, up to π, the negative of the angle at P3 subtending the same chord.
- So the sine vanishes exactly when the inscribed angles over P0P1 agree, i.e. when P0, P1, P2, P3 are concyclic.

Step 1 (sine rule, from projecting a triangle perpendicular to one side).
Write P0→P2 = P0→P1 + P1→P2 and take the component perpendicular to φ02:
r12 sin(φ02−φ12) = r01 sin(φ01−φ02).
Likewise, from P0→P3 = P0→P1 + P1→P3, with φ31 = φ13+π:
r13 sin(φ31−φ03) = r01 sin(φ01−φ03).

Step 2 (substitute these sines).
Ω = 1/(r12 r13 r23) · {r13 sin(φ01−φ02)cos(φ31−φ03) + r12 sin(φ01−φ03)cos(φ02−φ12)}.

Step 3 (projections along a side).
- Along φ03: r13 cos(φ31−φ03) = r01 cos(φ01−φ03) − r03.
- Along φ02: r12 cos(φ02−φ12) = r02 − r01 cos(φ01−φ02).

Step 4 (substitute and collect).
Ω = 1/(r12 r13 r23) · { r01[sin(φ01−φ02)cos(φ01−φ03) − sin(φ01−φ03)cos(φ01−φ02)] + r02 sin(φ01−φ03) − r03 sin(φ01−φ02) }.

Step 5.
The bracket equals sin((φ01−φ02)−(φ01−φ03)) = sin(φ03−φ02). Hence
Ω = { r01 sin(φ03−φ02) + r02 sin(φ01−φ03) + r03 sin(φ02−φ01) } / (r12 r13 r23).
W.Z.B.W. (= Q.E.D.)

Meaning (my addition). The final form uses only the polar coordinates (r0k, φ0k) of P1, P2, P3 as seen from P0, together with the mutual distances among P1, P2, P3.
- Invert about P0: w_k = e^{iφ0k}/r0k.
- The numerator equals 2·r01 r02 r03 × the signed area of the triangle w1 w2 w3.
- So Ω = 0 iff the inverted points are collinear, iff the four points are concyclic. This is consistent with Step 0.
The formula therefore gives a symmetric 'observer-centred' expression for the non-concyclicity of four points. This is the kind of quantity that matters, for example, in the Snellius–Pothenot resection problem, which fails on the 'danger circle'. This connection is my conjecture; the purpose is not stated on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Every step checks.
The overloaded notation, (ij) as both a length and an angle, is Gauss's and is used consistently.
The sign before (03) in Step 4 is blotted in the manuscript. It must be minus, as the transcription has it, for the final line to follow, and with minus the final line is correct.
In line 3 Gauss omits the double parentheses (writes 31−03 for (31)−(03)) — only abbreviation.

results.what: Projection (sine-rule) identities r12 sin(φ02−φ12) = r01 sin(φ01−φ02) and r13 cos(φ31−φ03) = r01 cos(φ01−φ03) − r03 for a triangle written with directed side directions
results.modern_name: law of sines / projection formula in vector-component form

results.what: Symmetric transformation: sin(φ02−φ12+φ31−φ03)/(r01 r23) = [r01 sin(φ03−φ02) + r02 sin(φ01−φ03) + r03 sin(φ02−φ01)]/(r12 r13 r23), a measure of deviation of four points from a common circle
results.modern_name: concyclicity criterion (inscribed-angle condition), equivalent to the inversion/Ptolemy-type condition
results.usually_credited_to: classical concyclicity criteria (Euclid, Ptolemy); this specific identity is an elementary trigonometric reformulation

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary plane-trigonometric verification, using the addition theorem and triangle projections, of an identity Gauss had stated on an earlier page. It is careful and correct but routine. It may belong to his geodetic or resection work, and the concyclicity connection is only my reading.

checkable.sympy: z0,z1,z2,z3 = 0.3+0.1j, 2.1+0.7j, 1.4+2.9j, -0.8+1.6j; import cmath; P=[z0,z1,z2,z3]; r=lambda i,j: abs(P[j]-P[i]); f=lambda i,j: cmath.phase(P[j]-P[i]); from math import sin,cos; abs(r(1,2)*sin(f(0,2)-f(1,2)) - r(0,1)*sin(f(0,1)-f(0,2))) < 1e-12
